questions.question: Use the check-supplier-invoice skill: can Zava Matériaux's invoice FA-2026-0217 be paid as it stands?

answer.text:
Non — pour le chantier Moreau, la facture FA-2026-0217 ne doit pas être payée telle quelle : elle facture 10 palettes de blocs ZM-20450 alors que le bon de livraison annoté indique seulement « reçu 8 pal. » et « 2 palettes manquantes » ; l’écart à traiter est donc 158,40 € HT, soit 190,08 € TTC à 20 % de TVA.[1][2] As of compte rendu de chantier n°3 du 24/03/2026, Bertrand Sauzède devait vérifier cette facture avant paiement.[3]

| Ligne | Facturé | Reçu / contrôlé | Différence | Montant en litige HT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ZM-20450 — blocs béton creux | 10 palettes à 79,20 € HT, total 792,00 € HT.[1] | Bon imprimé : 10 palettes, mais annotations de réception : 8 palettes reçues et 2 palettes manquantes ; preuve OCR à manier avec prudence.[2] | 2 palettes facturées non reçues | 2 × 79,20 € = 158,40 € HT.[1][2] |
| ZM-31020 — mortier | 30 sacs à 7,90 € HT, total 237,00 € HT.[1] | 30 sacs sur le bon.[2] | Pas d’écart constaté sur la quantité | 0,00 € HT.[1][2] |
| ZM-44108 — acier HA 10 | 24 barres à 9,45 € HT, total 226,80 € HT.[1] | 24 barres sur le bon.[2] | Pas d’écart constaté sur la quantité | 0,00 € HT.[1][2] |
| ZM-27340 — linteau béton | 1 unité à 164,00 € HT, total 164,00 € HT.[1] | 1 unité sur le bon.[2] | Pas d’écart constaté sur la quantité | 0,00 € HT.[1][2] |
| Frais de livraison camion-grue | 1 forfait à 65,00 € HT.[1] | Le bon indique une livraison par camion-grue.[2] | Pas d’écart constaté sur l’existence de la livraison | 0,00 € HT.[1][2] |

La facture totalise 1 484,80 € HT, 296,96 € de TVA à 20 %, et 1 781,76 € TTC.[1] Le montant litigieux est 158,40 € HT + 31,68 € de TVA = 190,08 € TTC, donc le montant payable après correction serait 1 326,40 € HT, 265,28 € de TVA et 1 591,68 € TTC si aucun autre écart n’est relevé.[1][2] Il faut obtenir de Zava Matériaux un avoir ou une facture corrigée pour les 2 palettes manquantes avant paiement.[1][2][3]

## 1) Progress by task — items to check first

The tasks already complete in the current planning are installation de chantier, terrassement, fondations, and dallage, all shown at **100%**, with the dallage noted as poured on **12/03/2026**. [2]

[3]

The works planned to start on the meeting date are **Électricité 1er œuvre**, planned **07/04/2026–10/04/2026**, and **Ouverture du mur existant / baie de liaison**, planned **07/04/2026–09/04/2026**, both shown at **0%** in the current planning. [4]

The later sequence remains isolation and plasterboard from **13/04/2026–24/04/2026**, kitchen removal and plumbing from **27/04/2026–30/04/2026**, second-fix electricity from **04/05/2026–06/05/2026**, tiling and faience from **04/05/2026–07/05/2026**, kitchen furniture installation from **11/05/2026–12/05/2026**, finishes and cleaning on **13/05/2026**, and reception on **15/05/2026**. [5]

## 2) Deliveries

The current planning shows **Livraison des menuiseries** by **VanArsdel Menuiseries** on **30/03/2026**, with **BC-2026-009** in the observations and **0%** progress at the schedule’s status date. [6]

I did not verify supplier emails or purchase-tracking rows within the available tool-call limit, so the meeting should specifically ask whether VanArsdel delivered the joinery and whether any delay affects the joinery installation and the start of first-fix electricity.

## 3) Open actions from site meeting no. 3

The previous site meeting was **site meeting no. 3** for the Moreau chantier, held on **24/03/2026 at 08:30** at **12 chemin des Vergers, Valbrise**. [7]

The action I could verify is that **Inès Roux** had to update **planning PLN-2026-003 to indice B** by **27/03/2026**. [8]

I did not find the resulting indice B in the wiki, so for meeting no. 4 this should be treated as an open point: confirm whether indice B exists, distribute it, and use it to replace indice A if issued.

## 4) Changes / amendments to follow

The schedule already includes the **fenêtre de toit** in the task **“Charpente, couverture et fenêtre de toit”**, and the lot column ties that task to **lot 4 and avenant n°1**. [9]

I did not verify any additional client change request not covered by an amendment, so meeting no. 4 should ask whether any new request after 24/03/2026 needs a formal avenant.

## 5) Suggested points to decide on 7 April 2026

Decide whether the masonry walls, roof / roof window, joinery delivery, and joinery installation are actually complete or delayed, because each is scheduled before 07/04/2026 and is not complete in the current planning. [3]

Decide whether first-fix electricity and the opening of the existing wall can start as planned on **07/04/2026**, because both tasks are scheduled to start that day. [4]

Decide whether the missing **planning indice B** must be issued before further coordination, because meeting no. 3 required Inès Roux to update the planning to indice B by **27/03/2026**. [8]

answer.text:

As of the crew schedule established on 03/04/2026, the week of 13 April 2026 is week 16: on **Chantier Moreau**, Mathis Ancelin, Kévin Rabaste and Anthony Lescoffier are assigned from 2026-04-13 to 2026-04-17 to insulation and plasterboard work on the extension, task T11.[1][2][3] On **Chantier résidence Les Nacrines**, Sébastien Quintard and Nordine Saadaoui are assigned from 2026-04-13 to 2026-04-17 to clearing reserves R04 and R07 and dismantling scaffolding.[4][5] Also on **Chantier résidence Les Nacrines**, Mathis Ancelin is assigned on 2026-04-16 and 2026-04-17 to reserve R02, repairing the 3rd-floor balcony nose from the MAT-04 boom lift.[6]

Yes, there is a scheduling conflict: **Mathis Ancelin** is booked on **Chantier Moreau** from 2026-04-13 to 2026-04-17 and also on **Chantier résidence Les Nacrines** on 2026-04-16 and 2026-04-17, so the overlap is **16–17 April 2026**.[1][6]
